name: Inkjection FR
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite, the block at the foot of the frame and every number in it
are the same and are named here rather than restated. What makes this
show itself is one sentence long - it is set in Texturina, in one
navy, on the photograph itself with no card under it - and everything
below is that sentence.
The FR in the name is the account's, the way the DE in Hall of Femme
DE is and the FR in Soccer Stories FR: it says which of the brand's
feeds this is and not what language the app is in. What lands on the
frames is whatever the video's own voice track was saying, put
through the transcription and the rewrite exactly as on every channel
here; nothing in this pack changes that, and everything the app
itself says is English like the rest of it (see CLAUDE.md).
One thing this pack checked that most of its siblings had no reason
to, and that the two DE feeds checked before it. Both Texturina files
carry 634 codepoints and cover what French actually needs - the acute
and the grave, the circumflex on all five vowels, the cedilla, the
diaeresis, the o-e ligature, and the angle quotes French sets speech
in - so a caption is drawn from the file rather than from whatever
the browser substitutes for a missing glyph, which would be a
different face at a width nothing measured. Worth stating because a
face chosen for how it looks in English is not automatically a face
that can SET another language, and the check is two minutes against a
cmap.
A folder of its own rather than a second colourway of Hall of Femme,
for the reason oh-my-goal-news is a folder of its own: the person
picking a channel at the top of the app picks this one or that one
and never both, and these two do not merely disagree about colour -
they are set in different type and one of them has no card at all,
which is as far as two packs under one heading go.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading: it is set
in Texturina Regular, in one navy, with a picked word in Texturina
Bold - and it is set on the PHOTOGRAPH, with no card behind it.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals,
where the block stands on the frame, what picking a word covers - is
the Snapchat caption design and is stated once, in
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack states what makes it
this show, and then states the two keys that the missing card forces
(`shadow` here and `shadow` inside `highlight`), each of which says
why it is an exception rather than a preference.
The face is the brand and the ground is what makes it difficult. A
serif at caption size over a still nobody chose the contrast of is
the hardest thing this app asks of a typeface: the hairlines that
make it a serif are exactly the strokes a photograph eats, and at
40px there is not much of them. Two things answer it. The file is the
18pt optical cut, which is the drawing of Texturina made for reading
rather than for a headline and therefore the one whose thins have
some body to them (see texturina-18pt-regular.json). And the type
carries a halo instead of a drop shadow, which is the `shadow` key
below.
Compare the three ways this heading has held a caption legible, since
this is now the third. Hall of Femme and most of its neighbours put
the words on a solid card, which is a ground somebody chose. Laugh
Society throws a dark scrim up from the foot of the frame and sets
white type on it. This channel does neither - the picture is left
whole, and the separation is bought one letter at a time.

_comment_color: A dark navy, and it is the whole palette rather than the first of
several: this show is set in one colour. It is therefore also
what every frame is drawn in, since a frame stores no colour of
its own until it is given one and there is no swatch here to give
Navy and not black, and on a channel with no card the difference
is not decoration. Black type on a photograph reads as something
punched out of the picture; a navy this deep is still
unmistakably dark at a glance, and carries a colour the eye can
name once it looks - which is what makes the caption belong to a
brand rather than to the player.
_comment_colors: Absent, and that is the palette being stated rather than
forgotten. Every other pack under this heading offers rows of
swatches because its look IS the pairing - which of its colours
is the card and which is the type. This show has one colour and
no card, so there is no pairing to offer and nothing for a second
Left unstated rather than written as a list of one, because a row
of one swatch is a control that cannot change anything: it draws
the colour already on screen, marked as chosen, and clicking it
does nothing a user can see. That is the one kind of control this
panel does not have anywhere (see the note on `alignable` in
js/editor.js). With no list the whole block of colour rows is
hidden instead - see editor.paletteOf, which hides a row whose
colours have nothing to recolour, and renderColorButtons, which
drops the block when no row survives.
Nothing counts these lists, so the day this show wants a second
colour it is one key in this file and the row appears.
_comment_shadow: An exception to the preset, and the first of the two the missing
card forces.
The preset states no shadow, and its reasoning is exact: there is
a solid slab under those letters in a colour the user picked, it
separates them from the photograph completely, and a shadow as
well would only smear the inside of the card. Take the card away
and every word of that stops being true - these letters are on a
photograph, with grain and edges and whatever was behind the
subject running through them.
So a shadow, and it is a LIGHT one, which no other pack here has.
The dark drop shadow every channel uses works because its type is
white: a dark edge under a light letter is contrast. This type is
navy. A black shadow under a navy letter is dark on dark - it
adds nothing on a bright still and is invisible on a dark one,
which is precisely the frame where the caption is already in
trouble. What dark type needs is a light ground, and with no card
to put one on, the ground is carried by the letters themselves: a
white halo, tight enough to read as a glow around the type rather
than as a shape behind it.
It is also why this channel throws no scrim (see `branding`
below). A scrim darkens the foot of the frame, which is the right
answer for white type and exactly the wrong direction for this.
No offset, in either axis. An offset shadow is cast by something
standing off a surface, and these letters are not standing off
anything; centred, it is light coming off them, which is what
holds a letter on all four sides rather than on two of them. 18px
of blur is what it takes to find an edge under a serif's thins at
40px without the halo becoming a visible white smudge - a couple
of pixels would show around the stems and nowhere else, and the
stems are not the strokes that go missing.
0.9 rather than 1: a hard white would put a second outline round
every letter and the caption would read as a sticker. Just under
opaque is a glow.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Texturina Bold, in the same navy as the
rest of the block. The highlight here is WEIGHT, which is Hall of
Femme's answer rather than Laugh Society's: one family, two cuts,
the change of voice being a change of volume and nothing else.
400 against 700 is the ordinary text pairing, and it is the right
one for this face - Texturina's Bold is drawn as the emphasis its
own Regular takes, and the two set on one line at the same cap
height with about five percent between their widths (both
measured in texturina-18pt-bold.json). That the cap heights are
identical matters more here than on a channel with a card: there
is no slab edge to measure the line against, so a picked word
riding even slightly high would be visible as a fault in the
sentence rather than as emphasis in it.
The colour it names is the block's, so the recolour draws exactly
what its neighbours are drawn in and the weight is the whole of
the difference. Stated all the same, for the reason `color` above
is stated - a highlight that changed colour as well as weight
would be two highlights, and this show has one navy.
The shadow is the second key the missing card forces, and unlike
the first it would be a bug rather than a weakness if it were
left out. The skeleton's own highlight shadow is a dark halo
meant to sit under a filled box (see BASE_TITLE_STYLE in
js/channels.js), and the preset overrides the block's shadow
without touching it - so a picked word would come out carrying a
BLACK halo while every word either side of it carried a white
one. Restated here to the number, so the whole sentence lifts off
the photograph the same way whether a word is picked out or not.
The mode and the scope come from the preset, which is where the
argument for picking out words rather than lines lives.
_comment_panel: None, and its absence is this channel's whole design. Written as
null rather than left out, which is the opposite of what
laugh-society-snapchat does and is right for the opposite reason:
that pack inherits nothing, so a key restating the skeleton's own
null would read as a slab somebody had switched off. This one
takes the Snapchat caption preset, and the preset states a card -
its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow. Null here is
what removes it, and it has to be said out loud.
There is no `colors.panel` either, so the swatch row that fills a
card on every sibling is not drawn at all rather than drawn dead

_comment_branding: No dark gradient, which is what every pack under this heading says,
but not for their reason - they have a card between the type and the
photograph and this one does not.
The reason here is the direction. The backend's gradient is a dark
ramp baked into the picture to hold LIGHT type legible, and this
channel's type is navy: darkening the frame under it closes the one
gap the caption is relying on. The whole of this pack's answer to
legibility is the white halo in `title.shadow`, which works by making
the letters lighter at their edges rather than the picture darker
behind them - and a shade thrown over the foot of the frame would
No `scrim` either, and for the same sentence: Laugh Society's shade
is the right answer for white type on a photograph and the wrong one
for dark type on the same photograph.
